:::{#exm-vcov-psd}
#### Two variance matrices that differ only in sign

Let $\vX = \tp{(X_1, X_2)}$ be equally likely to be each of the four points

$$D_1 = \set{(-5, 1),\ (0, -1),\ (0, 1),\ (5, -1)},$$

and let $\vX'$ be equally likely to be each of the four points

$$D_2 = \set{(5, 1),\ (0, -1),\ (0, 1),\ (-5, -1)}.$$

Both sets have first coordinates $\set{-5, 0, 0, 5}$
and second coordinates $\set{1, -1, 1, -1}$,
so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{X_1} &= \E{X_2} \\
&= 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{X_1^2} &= (25 + 0 + 0 + 25)/4 \\
&= 12.5,
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{X_2^2} &= (1 + 1 + 1 + 1)/4 \\
&= 1,
\end{aligned}
$$

and likewise for $\vX'$.
They differ in the products of the coordinates:

$$
\ba
\E{X_1 X_2} &= \frac{(-5)(1) + (0)(-1) + (0)(1) + (5)(-1)}{4} \\
&= -2.5, \\
\E{X_1' X_2'} &= \frac{(5)(1) + (0)(-1) + (0)(1) + (-5)(-1)}{4} \\
&= 2.5.
\ea
$$

Since the means are 0, @thm-vcov-elements and @thm-alt-cov give:

$$
\Varf{\vX} = \pmat{12.5 & -2.5 \\ -2.5 & 1},
\qquad
\Varf{\vX'} = \pmat{12.5 & 2.5 \\ 2.5 & 1}.
$$

Both are symmetric.
@thm-var-lincom with $\va = \tp{(1, 1)}$ and $\va = \tp{(1, -1)}$ gives:

$$
\ba
\Var{X_1 + X_2} &= 12.5 + 1 + 2(-2.5) &
\Var{X_1 - X_2} &= 12.5 + 1 - 2(-2.5) \\
&= 8.5, &
&= 18.5, \\
\Var{X_1' + X_2'} &= 12.5 + 1 + 2(2.5) &
\Var{X_1' - X_2'} &= 12.5 + 1 - 2(2.5) \\
&= 18.5, &
&= 8.5.
\ea
$$

As a check, $X_1 + X_2$ takes the values $-4, -1, 1, 4$,
each with probability $1/4$,
so its mean is 0 and its variance is $(16 + 1 + 1 + 16)/4 = 8.5$.

:::
